title: Customer registration, login and basket
context: A visitor registers as a customer, logs in to receive an authentication token, and uses that token to manage their shopping basket. Each customer has exactly one basket. Covers registration rules, the login token, adding an item to one's own basket, and isolation between different customers' baskets (story.md#L19-L22).
actors: customer (registered, logged in with a Bearer token)

sourcesRead.contributes: context, AC-1..AC-6 table, out of scope, PO comment with password rules
endpoints, request/response shapes, Bearer auth, duplicate e-mail error

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Registering with a unique e-mail, a rule-compliant password (sent as both `password` and `passwordRepeat`), and a security question id + security answer creates the customer: the response is **HTTP 201** and its body describes the new user with the submitted `email` and `role` = `customer`.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Registering with a unique e-mail, a rule-compliant password (sent as both password and passwordRepeat), and a security question id + security answer creates the customer: the response is HTTP 201 and its body describes the new user with the submitted email and role = customer.
outcomes: body data.email equals the submitted e-mail

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Registering with an e-mail that already belongs to a customer is rejected with **HTTP 400** and a validation error whose message states the e-mail must be unique. No second account is created.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Registering with an e-mail that already belongs to a customer is rejected with HTTP 400 and a validation error whose message states the e-mail must be unique. No second account is created.
outcomes: second registration with the same e-mail → HTTP 400
validation error whose message states the e-mail must be unique

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Registration enforces the password rules in the PO comment: a password shorter than the minimum length is rejected with **HTTP 400** and the customer is **not** created (a follow-up login with that e-mail/password fails).
acceptanceCriteria.text: Registration enforces the password rules in the PO comment: a password shorter than the minimum length (5 characters) is rejected with HTTP 400 and the customer is not created (a follow-up login with that e-mail/password fails).
outcomes: the customer is not created: a follow-up login with that e-mail/password fails

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Logging in via `POST /rest/user/login` with a registered customer's correct e-mail and password returns **HTTP 200** and a body containing an authentication **token** (a JWT used as a `Bearer` token) and the customer's basket id (`bid`).
acceptanceCriteria.text: Logging in via POST /rest/user/login with a registered customer's correct e-mail and password returns HTTP 200 and a body containing an authentication token (a JWT used as a Bearer token) and the customer's basket id (bid).
outcomes: body authentication.token is present and is a JWT
body authentication.bid (the customer's basket id) is present

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Using their own token, a customer can add a product to their own basket via `POST /api/BasketItems`; after that customer logs in through the UI, the basket page at `/#/basket` lists that product with the quantity that was added.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Using their own token, a customer can add a product to their own basket via POST /api/BasketItems; after that customer logs in through the UI, the basket page at /#/basket lists that product with the quantity that was added.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: UI login (route not stated, see G1), then the basket page at /#/basket
outcomes: POST /api/BasketItems with the customer's own token and own bid adds the product to that basket
after the customer logs in through the UI, /#/basket lists that product
the listed quantity equals the quantity that was added

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Basket contents are private to their owner: a customer must be able to read only their **own** basket. A request to `GET /rest/basket/{id}` authenticated as customer A but targeting customer B's basket id must be refused and must not return B's basket. Verify with two customers you create.

A request to GET /rest/basket/{id} authenticated as customer A but targeting customer B's basket id must be refused and must not return B's basket. Verify with two customers you create.
outcomes: customer A can read A's own basket via GET /rest/basket/{A's bid}
GET /rest/basket/{B's bid} with A's token is refused
that response does not return B's basket (not B's basket id, UserId or Products)

rules.text: The password must be at least 5 characters long; anything shorter than 5 characters must be rejected at registration and the account not created.
The password must be at most 40 characters long (no status or message stated for a longer password; no AC exercises it).
Treat the password as case-sensitive and store it hashed; per the PO this is not to be tested beyond a too-short password being refused.
Each customer has exactly one basket.

errorModel.case: Registering with an e-mail that already belongs to a customer: validation error whose message states the e-mail must be unique (exact wording not stated, see G6)
Registering with a password shorter than the minimum length (5 characters); the customer is not created
GET /rest/basket/{id} authenticated as customer A targeting customer B's basket id: refused, B's basket not returned (status not stated, see G4)

auth.mechanism: Authorization: Bearer <token>, where token is the JWT returned by POST /rest/user/login in authentication.token
auth.credentials: customers created by the tests themselves: unique e-mail per run, password from environment variable JS_USER_PASSWORD

testData.strategy: Tests create their own customers via POST /api/Users with a unique e-mail per run; the password comes from environment variable JS_USER_PASSWORD (satisfies the password rules). Security-question ids from GET /api/SecurityQuestions; product ids from GET /api/Products. AC-6 uses two customers created by the test.
constraints: password from JS_USER_PASSWORD (well above the 5-character minimum)
AC-3 reject cases use a 3- or 4-character password

outOfScope: testing that the password is case-sensitive and stored hashed (story.md#L51)
